item approach. Strategy number one to estimating rehab costs is working with general
contractors. General contractors are licensed professionals who can manage or have a crew to
renovate the entire fix and flip project as opposed to subcontractors who specialize in one type
of trade such as electrical or doing roofs. A great reason to use general contractors to get
renovation quotes is because you're working with a licensed professional who estimates rehab
costs for a living. They should be familiar with putting together a detailed quote you can use
to negotiate a contract on a potential deal. Also, having a quote from a professional licensed
contractor will add credibility when it comes time to ask for a price reduction on homes you
might be negotiating as opposed to you telling an agent or seller what you think it's going to
cost. It makes it hard for someone to dispute the cost of renovations when it's coming from a
licensed contractor as opposed to a biased investor who of course wants to show the highest
possible renovation cost. This method should be used by new investors as well as investors who
have long-standing relationships with contractors you can rely on and offload the timeconsuming
work of putting together a quote onto somebody else. When I first moved to South Carolina, I
picked a specific neighborhood I was going to live in and renovate. And to get my contractor

driving around and meeting subcontractors and asking them if they can introduce me to the

contractors to work with. Number one, go to your local real estate group where there are

will give you a detailed estimate, including material and labor, and what it's going to cost to
complete that project. Step number three, take your detailed quote and use it to negotiate a

you expect the work to be done. Now, let's talk about strategy number two, estimating

renovate to find out how much it will cost to renovate that home. Now, this is an average based
on the condition of the home. Overall homes in good shape that just need a little bit of
flooring and paint can be an average of $10 a square foot. If the home is in overall good shape,
but is really outdated, then we can estimate our average level of renovation, which comes out to
about $30 a square foot. And finally, if the home is in horrible shape and everything needs to
be done, as a quick guide, the cost will be about $60 per square foot. as our total renovation
budget. You do not have to spend hours analyzing a property. You can spend seconds or minutes.
This method should be used by everybody, especially wholesalers and fix and flippers. Whether

steps on how to use the square footage method to estimate rehab costs. Step number one,
determine the property square footage. You can do this by asking your real estate agent,
checking on Redf Fin or Zillow to see how many square foot the house is. But be careful because
it's not always accurate. Or you can check on county tax records, which are going to be your

detailed line item by line item approach. This approach is when you go through your scope of

every one of those items to come up with a total renovation cost. You can do this by calling
general contractors and subcontractors and ask what they would charge to do every part of your
scope of work. Unlike relying on a single contractor to give you a quote, with this method, you
can call different subcontractors for each line item and get quotes for each of them. This
method is best used for experienced professionals who have established relationships with many
contractors. That way, you can call different contractors for each part of your scope of work to
get the best pricing. Or you already know from having existing relationships what each one of
them charges for each part of your scope of work. For example, whenever I am buying a renovation
and coming up with a budget for that project, I can call multiple electricians if the entire
house needs to be rewired and let them compete against each other through bidding on that part
of the project. Let's go through the four steps of how to do the line item by line item
approach. Step number one, write a detailed scope of work, which again is a list of everything
you want done at the house. Step number two, if you're new, you have to build a list of multiple
contractors if you don't already have one for each one of those line items, such as three
electricians to give you electrical rewiring quotes. Step number three, either meet different
contractors at the home to show them what you want done, or if possible, send them a detailed
description and ask them if they can give you an estimate based on pictures and a detailed scope

with a total renovation budget. Now that we talked about three ways of estimating your rehab
cost, let's go over three common mistakes investors make when creating their renovation budget.
Mistake number one, when you're estimating rehab cost, you underestimate your renovation budget.
This mistake happens when investors purposely lower their total budget to try to make the deal
work and expect their contractors and project managers to figure out how to make that number
work. And because project managers and contractors rarely know how to make that type of magic
happen, it's better to use the renovation budget that a contractor gives you and that you come
up with using the detailed line item by line item process. Our second mistake that beginners
make when estimating the rehabs is overlooking hidden issues. This mistake happens when
investors do a simple walkthrough by themselves or with a contractor to come up with a scope of
work and do not look in the attic, under the house, and all the other nooks and crannies where
all the hidden issues could be hiding. Besides walking through the house with an experienced
professional who knows what they're looking at, make sure to do a full home inspection, a
termite inspection, and if you live in some parts of the country, do a radon inspection during
your due diligence or before you buy the house. Because project managers and contractors rarely
know how to make that type of magic happen. To avoid this mistake, it's better to use the
renovation budget that a contractor gives you or that you came up with using the detailed line
item by line item process. Mistake number three when estimating rehab costs is having a lack of
contingency funds. This is a mistake that investors make when they come up with a cost to do
their project that doesn't take into account extra money to cover unforeseen or unexpected
issues during the renovation process. No matter how detailed of an inspection you do, there is
no way to avoid extra costs that might come up from such things such as theft, maybe a
contractor dropping expensive material and breaking it or issues coming up behind closed walls.
You would never know unless you rip the walls open, which of course you can't do unless you own
the home. And to avoid this mistake, depending on the size of the project, you should always
build in a minimum of 10% of contingency budget if it's a small renovation. and up to 25% if
it's a major rip it apart down to the studs and start over renovation. To recap, let's go over
